deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 9-11). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a category M of 'standard cells', one object I_n per dimension n, in which all maps are face inclusions. M is reduced: isomorphic objects are equal. He shows M can be recovered from purely combinatorial data, called M_0:
- the ordered set N;
- for each n, an ordered set I_n (the face poset of the n-cell) with a greatest element d_n;
- a strictly increasing 'dimension' map τ_n : I_n → N with image N_{≤n} and τ_n^{-1}(n) = {d_n};
- for each face ξ of dimension n' = τ_n(ξ), an injection ξ ↦ u^n_ξ : I_{n'} → I_n, which is an isomorphism onto the lower set (I_n)_{≤ξ};
- a cocycle condition: u^n_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η = u^n_{u^n_ξ(η)}.
In modern terms, M is a direct (Reedy-type) category with all maps monic, in which each slice M/I_n is the poset I_n with terminal object d_n. Every face of a cell is canonically again a standard cell.

This page.
1. The converse: such data define a category M_0 satisfying his axioms (i) and (ii).
2. NB: in the intended cases the indexing set is N itself.

The three examples.
- Ex. 1, simplices. Finite totally ordered sets [0,n] (the simplices Δ_n) with strictly increasing maps. This is the semi-simplicial category Δ_+ (Δ_inj). Here I_n is the set of non-empty subsets of Δ_n, so card = 2^{n+1} − 1.
- Ex. 2, 'pinned' (épinglés) cubes. A cube is pinned by a total order on its set of pairs of opposite hyperfaces, plus a choice of a '+' hyperface in each pair. A pinning of a cube induces a pinning of each of its faces. Morphisms are pinning-preserving face inclusions, which gives the semi-cubical (face-only) cube category □_+. Here I_n is the set of faces of □^n, so card = 3^n.
- Ex. 3, hemispheres/globes D_n. J_n = (Δ × {±1}) ⊔ {d_n}, with {±1} 'chaotic' and d_n the greatest element. In dimension k < n there are exactly two faces D_k^±, and each is below every face of higher dimension. Hom(D_k, D_n) has two elements: iterated sources and targets. This is the face category of the globular site (globes without identities), and card J_n = 2n + 1.

Claim (a). For n ≥ 1 and J_n^* = J_n \ {d_n}:
- the geometric realization of the nerve |J_n^*| is an (n−1)-sphere;
- |J_n| = cone(|J_n^*|) is an n-disk.
In all three cases the proper-face posets are 'CW posets' in Björner's sense: posets that are the face posets of regular CW complexes.

The next page adds (b): the posets I_n^* are regular, i.e. flag-transitive. He asks: which sequences (P_n) of regular spherical polytopes have all lower intervals (P_n)_{≤ξ} ≅ P_{n'}? He remarks 'that must be in Coxeter'. The aim is a classification of all such 'shape categories' M; this presumably serves the stacks / test-category / higher-groupoid project of the same period (Pursuing Stacks era).
errors: Ex. 3 index slip: with card J_n = 2n+1 (margin), the factor must have n elements, i.e. Δ_{n−1} = [0,n−1], not Δ_n as in Ex. 1. With Δ_n as in Ex. 1, |J_n^*| would be S^n, not S^{n−1}.

Ex. 3 order: 'chaotic' (indiscrete) order on {±1} in a product would make (i,+) and (i,−) equivalent, so J_n would only be a preorder. What is needed is (i,ε) < (j,ε') iff i < j, with (i,+), (i,−) incomparable. That is the strict part of that preorder, or equivalently a lexicographic sum with discrete {±1}. This is a minor slip of wording.
Claim (a) is correct in all three cases. For the simplex and the cube, |J_n^*| is the barycentric subdivision of the boundary. For the globe, |J_n^*| is the join of n copies of S^0, which is S^{n−1}.
The page itself contains no proof; the claims are stated, but they are standard.

ideas.what: Encoding a reduced category of cells by face posets I_n with a dimension function and canonical face isomorphisms I_{n'} ≅ (I_n)_{≤ξ} satisfying a cocycle condition; the converse reconstruction
ideas.modern_name: direct / regular skeletal category whose slices M/x are posets with terminal object ('regular' shape category, face-category of a regular cell family)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; related notions in Cisinski (régulières squelettiques), Henry (regular polygraphs), Björner (CW posets)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses test categories built from simplices, cubes and similar shapes, but this exact axiomatization is not recalled there

ideas.what: Pinned cubes: total order on the pairs of opposite hyperfaces plus a choice of + face; induced pinning on faces gives a skeletal semi-cubical category
ideas.modern_name: semi-cubical site □_+ (face maps only, no symmetries)
ideas.where_published: cubes are discussed in Pursuing Stacks; the 'épinglage' formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Globes/hemispheres with two faces in each lower dimension, as a third example on the same footing as simplices and cubes
ideas.modern_name: globular site (reduced); face poset of the abstract regular polytope {2,2,...,2} (hosotope/ditope)
ideas.usually_credited_to: globular sets: Street, Batanin; Grothendieck's own 'hemispheres' in Pursuing Stacks
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (hemispheres D_n, globular structures / coherators)

ideas.what: Criterion: the realization of the proper-face poset is S^{n−1}, and the full poset is D^n
ideas.modern_name: CW poset / face poset of a regular CW ball

ideas.what: Flag-transitivity (next page) and the question of classifying families of regular polytopes closed under taking faces
ideas.modern_name: abstract regular polytopes / string Coxeter groups

missed.claim: Simplices, cubes and globes are treated uniformly as flag-transitive regular cell families. Implicitly, the globe D_n is the regular abstract polytope with Schläfli symbol {2,...,2}, with automorphism group (Z/2)^n. Grothendieck's question (with b)) then reduces to a classification problem. One needs infinite Schläfli strings p_1, p_2, ... all of whose initial segments give finite (spherical) Coxeter groups. The answer: a finite spherical prefix followed eventually by all 2's (globe-like), or by a component 3,3,3,... (A_∞) or 4,3,3,... (B_∞). So there are infinitely many families beyond simplex, cube and globe (e.g. {p,2,2,...}, {5,3,2,2,...}), but only these three tail types. Note: the cross-polytope {3,...,3,4} does not extend to a face-closed family.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a systematic catalogue of candidate 'shape categories' (regular direct categories of cells) for higher-categorical and homotopical models: simplicial, cubical, globular and hybrids. Such a catalogue does not seem to be stated in the test-category or polytopic literature in this Coxeter-theoretic form.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic framework for families of standard cells (simplices, cubes, globes) and asks for further examples. The project of classifying such cell categories and studying which of them give test categories was not completed here.
missed.quote: Inversement, de telles données définissent une catégorie M_0 satisfaisant à (i) (ii).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links to current work on which shape categories (Θ, cubes with connections, polytopic sites) model homotopy types or ω-categories. Most of this, however, is now well developed independently.

deep.surprise_reason: Every example and the sphere criterion are standard (CW posets, the semi-simplicial, semi-cubical and globular sites). What is mildly notable is the uniform 'regular polytope' viewpoint that puts globes alongside simplices and cubes, and the explicit classification question that ties shape categories to Coxeter theory. This seems not to be pursued in the literature in exactly this form, but it is not deep.
transcription_corrections: Margin (Ex. 2): roughly 'J_n = ens. des facettes du n-cube □^n ... card J_n = 3^n'; the transcribed 'sections ... d'ordre' is likely a misreading.
'hyperface entière +' is probably 'une hyperface notée +' (the choice of a + face in each pair).
'Ex 1 ... {+[0,n]+}' is an insertion above 'ens. finis', identifying the finite totally ordered sets with [0,n].
'N̄ = N': the bar is probably a struck or decorated N; the meaning is that the indexing ordered set of the data is N itself.
The poset symbol on this page should be read as the same script I_n as on the previous page (the transcription alternates between I_n and J_n).
